key_claims: The Muslim Brotherhood is the parent of Sunni Islamism; it uses terrorism where it works (Hamas) and patient civil-society infiltration where it does not (Britain), aiming at a global caliphate on a century timescale.
Al-Qaeda descends from Brotherhood splinters that killed Sadat; Zindani's Islah shows the incestuous AQ–Brotherhood overlap.
Western complacency (Cold War 'enemy's enemy' in Afghanistan, 'end of history' arrogance, Londonistan, Islamophobia charges) let the Brotherhood embed in the West.
The Iran war, which grew out of 7 October, has slowed but not halted US designations of Brotherhood branches; al-Islah may be next.
Sectarian lines are blurring: the Iranian axis now includes al-Qaeda (leader in Iran) and Hamas; Qatar's break with Hamas and tensions inside Al Jazeera are things to watch.
